desc:
Great round stones covered entirely in light-green crusted lichen rest deep in
the harsh earth on steep forested slopes. Tall oaks and firs loom over the
sunken boulders to create an eternally dark wasteland of hard cold stone and dry
cracked soil. Ragged and withered undergrowth barely cling to life amidst
parched dust under the choking forest canopy.
name: Boulder-strewn Forested Mountainside

desc:
A huge, forlorn tree grows amidst the mountains with its enormous branches
reaching high above the rest of the uneven canopy along the low peaks. The great
trunk plunges seemingly into the very stone of the mountain top, its titanic
roots cracking and splitting rock in every direction. The ground surrounding the
hulking tree is rugged with many boulders covering what little topsoil remains.
name: Massive Forlorn Tree

desc:
Large flat slabs of rock cover the slope that rises to the north. Gaps between
the stone create sudden explosions of tree growth. Great dark firs and oaks
appear rampant wherever breeches in the granite permit, their great boughs
reaching toward one another to block out the sky above.
name: Slab-covered Slope

desc:
The small mountaintop is dominated by burnt oak trees encircling a tiny glade
still entirely covered by intertwined, scorched branches. Both bark and bough
are charred to a uniform colour blacker than night itself. The forest seems to
hiss constantly from every direction, the air thick with malice and hostility.
name: Burned, Blackened Glade

desc:
A wide rocky cave has been turned into an orkish camp. Several charred pieces of
lumber lie against the northern wall of a cave, right next to a midden which is
littered with bones. A few large rocks frame the back of the cave, used as
makeshift seats next to a large cooking pot. The pot lies on its side towards
the back of the cave, its contents emptied.
name: Orkish Camp

desc:
Amidst hoary trees wounded with the hacking of axes lies a large, round stump, a
decaying remnant of a bygone era in the history of Mirkwood. Its dead roots
sprawl in every direction and all around the ground are scattered dark green
leaves. Even with meagre light, the girdle of oaks cast an imposing shadow on
the forest beyond. The dark surface of the trees struggle to reflect any light.
Webs stretch between the very tops of the trees, hanging ready for the return of
their masters.
name: Black Forest

desc:
Ancient oak trees with black bark stand here, timeless and still in the gloom of
Mirkwood. The thick forest-roof remains motionless as it imposes a suffocating
darkness upon that which it covers. Webs crawl up the trunks and weave among the
branches of the trees, burdening the canopy and further obscuring the roof of
the world. Amid rotten debris and long-fallen branches lies a hollow, ebony log
conquered by time and moss.
name: Depths of Mirkwood

desc:
Green, springy creepers meld with oozing mud to drag at every step through a
sodden morass in the centre of this valley. A dank, earthy odour permeates the
air, tinged with a hint of rot and decay. The thick sludge of the forest floor
appears to have suffocated all plant life except for hulking beeches and the
vines that cling to them.
name: Mirkwood Morass

desc:
Swarms of dead insects float on pitch-black water pooling in the depressions
between thick-girthed roots. Putrid mould blackens entire tree boles, stretching
upward from the foul water which seems to be its source. The air is suffocating,
thick with a noxious vapour which evaporates from the pools and mingles with an
oppressive stench of decay.
name: Mirkwood Morass

desc:
A thick sludge of rainwater, decaying fungi, and mouldy vegetation spreads over
the forest floor. Stunted beeches struggle to grow, their roots engulfed by the
viscous filth. Rotting creepers reach upward to latch onto writhing branches,
dragging them down to the ravenous morass.
name: Mirkwood Morass

desc:
A massive tree has fallen here, its death throes bringing down several of its
smaller brethren. Their rotting stumps are covered in patches of black mould and
vivid orange fungi. Large, grey beetles bore into the soft, decomposing bark to
feed on the wood at the core; they are surrounded by swarms of maggots which
devour the fungi at the surface. The ground beneath the trunk is damp and
marshy; it sags beneath the great weight of the dead tree.
name: Mirkwood Morass

desc:
A stream of water trickles over the edge of an opening high up a cliff to the
east. Its presence is obscured by a dense curtain of vines, and camouflaged by a
vibrant emerald moss that surrounds it. The water flows down leafy beech
branches stretching toward the cliff; it eventually meets the ground where it
mixes with decaying vegetation to form a viscid muck.
name: Sludge beneath a Cliff

desc:
Viscous mud drips from a looming overhang to the east. The rest of the sky is
blocked out by the thickly woven foliage of beeches that sprawl across the
valley. The leaves closest to the cliff are spattered with mud, as are various
boulders and rocks near the cliff. The ground is marshy and covered in a soft,
thick layer of mould.
name: Sludge beneath a Cliff

desc:
A plateau hangs over the valley from the east. Emerald moss stretches up the
steep face, nourished by water that seeps from cracks in a cliff wall. As this
water reaches the forest floor, it mixes with a thick, damp sludge composed of
decaying vegetation. Broad trunks of beech trees rise from this morass, their
distant crowns casting dark shadows.
name: Sludge beneath a Cliff

desc:
Heavy clouds of spores hang in the air around vivid fungi that line
broad-girthed beeches. The fruiting bodies exhibit various shades of green,
orange and red, visible wherever light peeks through the distant, obscuring
canopy. The damp air causes the spores to stick together in clearly visible
clumps, making it difficult to breathe.
name: Mirkwood Morass

desc:
The valley narrows suddenly as a rugged mountain juts into it from the north.
Birches blanketing the slope meet densely packed beeches that dominate the
valley floor. The beeches continue to thicken to the east, and headway in that
direction is only possible by following the northern slope of the valley.
name: Narrowing Valley

desc:
The beech and birch trees on the northern slope of the valley are stricken with
disease; their bores ooze amber sap. Fragile and rotten vines hang from drooping
branches. The sodden decaying vegetation on the incline provides little
purchase. The few patches of exposed rock are little better, as they are covered
in slippery, grey-green lichen.
name: Blighted Slope

desc:
The beeches in this valley lack most of their leaves, and large swaths of bark
are missing from their trunks. Soft, rotten remains of beech-bark lie on the
forest floor atop mounds of leaves, providing sustenance to a rampant ochre
fungus. The patchy canopy lets in more light than is typical for the murky
forest, revealing the cliffs that border the valley to the north and south.
name: Rotting Trees

desc:
Ochre mould blankets trunk, roots, and limbs of sickly beeches. No bark is
visible in the rare gaps devoid of fungi. The bare, drooping branches afford a
clear view of the steep valley walls to the north and south which extend for
several miles.
name: Rotting Trees

desc:
These beeches are dead, and have been for a long time. Leafless branches droop
from their trunks. The floor is a sodden mass of decomposing vegetation covered
in a thick layer of mould and fungus. Scattered squat and sickly shrubs struggle
to survive in the septic soil.
name: Rotting Trees

desc:
Countless rows of thick grey trunks extend beyond sight in the darkness beneath
the great canopy of Mirkwood. From each trunk sprouts twisted, bulbous roots
that intertwine with one another to form a hard, knotted floor that rises as it
approaches each tree and then falls again. Rigid boughs grow together from tree
to tree to form a confusing maze in the smothering lightless environment that
the boughs themselves help to create.
name: Forested Valley

desc:
The evergreen trees here block out all possibility of sunlight penetrating the
forest canopy. Twisted trunks and sickly plants dot the forest floor, serving as
living examples of the vanquished vegetation in the eternal war of the plants as
they struggle for life in the forest of Mirkwood. Steep rocks and sharp stones
rise up to the southwest.
name: Shadowy Forest

desc:
A treacherous forested slope rises to the west beneath an impenetrable canopy of
interwoven fir branches. The slope continues northward toward two towering stone
spires, leveling off into a valley toward the east. The ground is rocky with
sparse outcroppings of larger boulders wrapped in exposed tree roots.
name: Steep Wooded Slope

desc:
Disintegrating trees lie strewn across a steep slope which climbs to the south.
The slope becomes steeper and steeper until it rises vertically to the south and
becomes impassable. The slope is hemmed in by grey rock on either side and the
surrounding rock walls offer little opportunity for breeze or wind to disturb
the heavy odour of decay. The ground is soft and covered in mould, and there
seems to be nothing in the way of healthy vegetation; all has turned to rot.
name: Rotting Incline

desc:
Bulbous toadstools blanket the forest floor, thriving silently in the darkness
imposed by a thickly-woven canopy. Broken pieces ground into the earth betray
where creatures have traversed this region of the forest. The fungi sit on an
ample bed of decaying twigs and leaves mixed with sticky mud.
name: Mirkwood Morass

desc:
Dark green and black-speckled algae cover several small murky pools of water,
contrasted by a soft and damp forest floor, which is littered by splintered
pieces of wood and dead leaves. Beeches, stunted but with thick mouldy-covered
foliage grow on the drier spots of land. Wiry and gnarly roots stick out in
clumps in various spots, forming both sturdier footholds and barriers.
name: Mirkwood Morass

desc:
Long, narrow ridges protrude from a high escarpment to the west. Grey-green
lichen blankets these large, exposed rock faces. Stands of beeches thrive in the
narrow ravines between these ridges. Their stretching foliage obscures the
forest floor, reaching up to the height of the ridges. Gusts of wind send waves
through the canopy, making these ridges appear as if they were sandbars
breaching the surface of a rolling river.
name: Protruding Ridges

desc:
Two great stone spires tower up through the sparse canopy on the western and
eastern sides of a lightly wooded slope, reaching far above the forest floor
resting between them. Massive moss-covered trunks have burst through the cold
hard stone between the great pillars, their lichen-covered branches growing into
one another to form a thick layer of tangled vegetation that covers many parts
of the steep and rugged terrain near the ground.
name: Two Stone Spires

desc:
A rugged ridge curves from south to east, looming over a level valley which hugs
the steeply slanting slope. The bottom of the valley is filled with stout oaks
whose branches seem to rake at the slopes of the ridge. Little grows beneath the
cover of the branches which extend several dozen feet up the slope of the ridge.
However, a few scraggly shrubs take refuge higher up the slope, out of reach of
the trees.
name: Foot of a Ridge

desc:
A rugged slab of rock juts from a mountainside to the north and hangs above a
charred valley far below. It slants gently downward as it separates from the
mountainside. Debris fallen from above litters the surface of the slab. Some
large boulders rest precariously at the edges. Broad, jagged cracks zigzag
inward from the sides of the slab. It is unclear how deep these cracks run and
how many more impacts this overhang can weather.
name: Precarious Overhang

desc:
A sheer rock wall to the west stretches far above the highest reach of decrepit
oaks that appear to claw at its face. The cliff face is riven with cracks, and
gaping holes show where pieces of rock have broken off. Numerous rocks and
boulders lie in the shadows of the trees.
name: Beneath Fractured Precipices

desc:
The corner of a plateau towers over this part of Mirkwood, its steep cliffs
running south and west. Rocks and small boulders appear to have tumbled down
from the sheer plateau wall, creating jagged points in the rock as they crashed
their way to the forest floor below. A broad shelf cuts westward, mediator
between the plateau and a valley to the north.
name: Beneath Fractured Precipices

desc:
Crumbling cliffs surround a dense copse of beeches. Shattered boulders mingled
with splintered branches indicate the slow retreat of the trees. A few shrubs
and stunted saplings have taken tentative root along unshaded ledges on the rock
walls.
name: Beneath Fractured Precipices

desc:
A broad, level shelf runs along the base of a high plateau to the south.
Opposite to the cliff there is a steep dropoff several dozen feet to a forested
valley floor. A web of cracks stretches across the southern cliff wall, which is
fractured in several places. Large slabs and boulders lie strewn across the
shelf. To the west, the ledge tapers to an end; there the plateau descends to
the valley in a single unbroken fall.
name: Beneath Fractured Precipices

desc:
Tall fir trees tower over this rugged plateau. Bone-white strands of gossamer
lichen drape from their branches and seem to hover in the breezes that whisk
along the rows of trunks. Enormous, step-like rock formations climb up to a
rugged shelf that skirts the terrain to the northeast. A gaping rent scars the
centre of the plateau, leading down to a vast chasm.
name: Fir-Clad Plateau

desc:
This uplift in the land gazes west over a broad and dark valley. Fir trees
stretch over the precipice, outspread branches casting shadows far below.
Strands of grey hairlike lichen droop from the trees. Farther away from the
cliff, this lichen is more closely cropped, a sign of grazing.
name: Fir-Clad Plateau

desc:
Short, steep cliffs rim this region of the plateau. Ranks of young fir trees
tufted in grey lichen stand in the lee of the overhanging rocks. Large, mossy
boulders gaze above the trees, casting shadows over the saplings. Yellow grass
grows between mounds of rock, partially obscured by the dry needles that litter
the ground. An impressive pile of recently-felled trees, their needles still
green, rests in front of a bulge on the southern cliff wall.
name: Fir-Clad Plateau

desc:
Gnarled oak trees lean ominously over rocky scrambles that dominate the
mountainous landscape amid the forest. Large boulders cover the ground while
tangly vines weave their way along the tree trunks and around the great stones.
The rocky ground descends to the east even as the elevation increases to the
west.
name: Boulder-strewn Forest

desc:
Tall oak and fir trees reach to the unseen sky, blocking any possible light from
reaching the ground. Only a few small withered vines and scraggly bushes manage
to survive in such conditions on the ground itself amidst the choking atmosphere
of the massive dominating trees.
name: Dark Forest

desc:
A deep chasm with steep, slippery walls cuts this part of the Emyn-nu-Fuin off
from the mountains to the south and east. Ancient, gnarled trees grow up to the
very edge of the chasm, their trunks twisting this way and that as if attempting
to escape the strangling vines that ruthlessly encircle them. The canopy above
is dense enough to block out the sky. The light that finds its way along the
forest floor from the gap created by the chasm will never be enough to dispel
the gloom that lingers here.
name: Chasm Edge

desc:
The mountains of the Emyn-nu-Fuin climb toward the north-east as they slowly
transform into taller fir-clad peaks. The terrain is very rugged as deep chasms
and endless ravines clash with sudden cliff-walls rising up into the darkness of
the forest above. Amidst this inhospitable terrain, crooked trees and sprawling
bushes flourish amidst the cracks and crevices of the cold stone.
name: Jagged Crags of the Emyn-nu-Fuin

desc:
The fir trees here are hoary and overgrown with sickly coloured fungi that vary
in their grotesque shapes and contours. Tangles of thick vines snake up along
the trees, twisting around boles and branches. To the south, the terrain becomes
elevated as the trees are forced to grow among boulders and rocks, while to the
east the forest floor appears to descend.
name: Tangled Woodland

desc:
The great bent trees here appear to be sparse amid a gloomy depression. The
majority of the trees are covered by a damp, grey moss that smells strongly of
decay. The forest to the north and west appears to climb away off into the
horizon, while a single dark and narrow gap opens to the south covered in thick
sticky webs.
name: Depression in a Dark Forest

desc:
Great dark oaks and firs grow close together with boughs and branches
intertwining in every direction. Thick twisted roots weave their way along the
forest floor in a tangled web of strangling creepers. The shadowy woods extend
to the north, south, and east beneath the blackness of the unseen treetops until
they collide with steep mountain cliffs.
name: Forested Valley

desc:
Burrowing into the earth, this dark passageway is covered in unusually large
cobwebs. Sticky threads stretch taught forming layers of webbing around all but
the floor, which is covered in moist soil and some light vegetation that extends
from the forested depression to the north.
name: Webbed Recess

desc:
Thick, sticky webs cover every surface of the black tunnel. Nothing grows at
this depth along the hard tacky floor or on the milky white walls and ceiling.
The many tightly-woven strands of exceptionally strong silk are coated with a
clear liquid that clings immediately to anything that comes into contact with
it.
name: Webbed Tunnel

desc:
The web-covered route through the earth is covered in what appears to be a
single, thick pale web that suffocates every surface. Occasionally, a light
breeze issues from above causing some of the loose fibers along the walls and
ceiling to sway to and fro. The slightest touch of the webs here causes a
visible tremor to carry on eastward into the foreboding darkness.
name: Bend in a Webbed Tunnel

desc:
A winding webbed corridor winds its way underground amidst numerous pillars,
carved from the elements and time, standing fast as if to hold open the pallid
veins of the earth. Stones of various sizes protrude from the walls but are
veiled by thick webs that stretch to conquer all visible surfaces.
name: Threaded Tunnel

desc:
A narrow corridor winds its way through the bottom of a large canyon that rises
to the south. Large white cracks are visible along the steep dark walls of rock.
The canyon floor is barren but for a few weeds. Far above, the edges of the
forest canopy can be seen hanging over the top of the recess like the roof of a
black tunnel.
name: Bottom of a Black Canyon

desc:
Dark black moss grows along the sides of the canyon while rotting debris, fallen
from the overhanging forest above, covers the ground. A lone crag juts from the
otherwise soft soiled wall to the south. Fern and weed fill the moist floor,
unhindered by the surrounding decay.
name: Wet, Humid Canyon

desc:
Black weeds sprout from the moist floor amidst piles of foul-smelling fungi and
rotting plant matter. Thick strands of ominous webbing stretch between the
looming stone walls, though the canopy above is still visible between them.
Drops of moisture collect along the bottoms of the silken ropes and occasionally
drip down on the dark mouldy piles below.
name: Bend in a Humid Canyon

desc:
Shallow pools of black water have formed in the soft dark soil to form a hidden
bog. Tall weeds grow thick in sloppy mud surrounding each pool amidst the
darkness in the still wet air. The trunk of a dead ancient oak leans
precariously against the west wall, its narrow top having already sunk down into
a particularly large black morass. A foreboding rounded tunnel entrance leads
into the eastern wall of the canyon revealing only complete and utter blackness
in that direction.
name: Swampy Canyon

desc:
Decayed vegetation covers the wet, muddy floor of the deep crevice. The steep
passage narrows into a jagged fissure and an apparent dead-end to the south.
Thick webs crawl up the cleavage of the canyon, making passage possible only by
those fell creatures that produced the sticky strands. Dark vines hang from the
forest over the top of the crack as they strain to reach the rancid water below.
name: Bog in the Canyon

desc:
Rising high into the sky, imposing walls close in to form a narrow passage. Some
trees have managed to take root along the canyon floor in small clusters. The
space created by the fissure breaks up the forest canopy hanging far above. A
cleft looms ominously in the great stone wall to the west.
name: Steep Canyon

desc:
Uncounted stones fill the bottom of a steep incline, making it difficult for any
plant to take root in this area of the forest canyon. Rugged rock walls are
adorned with thick vegetation at the top of the crevice which sprouts dark vines
that hang down from the forest floor far above.
name: Rough Canyon

desc:
The cover of Mirkwood imposes itself over a canyon's narrow opening above as
branch and vine hang down ominously into the gaping chasm. The great dark walls
curve downward into a black soil as they form a narrow floor covered in dark
moss and fern growth.
name: Dark Canyon

desc:
Dark, ridged stone forms nearly vertical walls towering upward that block all
light from reaching this place. A cluster of gnarled oaks grows ravenously upon
one smooth area of soil, free from the loose rock and large boulders that
dominate most of the fissure's bottom. Loose stones and boulders give way to
dark moss and young ferns toward the east.
name: Sunless Chasm

desc:
A wide and deep crevice cleaving the hard bedrock beneath the soil of mirkwood
cuts its way down to form a steep slope toward the east. Debris made up of
decaying plant matter and cracked boulders lies piled here along the bottom of
the great crack in the earth, having fallen from far above over countless years
as it amassed to form an artificial floor.
name: Deep Fissure

desc:
A tiny recess in the stone carved by the elements, the rough ceiling of this
hollow provides some shelter from the open canyon to the east. Smooth grey walls
are disrupted by deep cracks that reveal veins of different types of rocks and
minerals. The floor is hard and barren but for a few grains of dirt.
name: Carved Hollow

desc:
A dense wall of trees rings a foetid pond that occupies the lowest depths of a
broad valley. The water of the pool absorbs all light, guarding the secret of
what lies beneath its surface. Several barren trunks of long-dead trees stand in
the midst of the toxic water. The roots nearest to the pond blacken and shrivel
as they carry poison back to their dying trees. A muddy slope to the west feeds
the pond with black, sticky mud.
name: Mirkwood Morass

desc:
Several clumps of dirt and small, round stones litter the bottom of the chasm,
which is framed by smooth, tall cliffs that impede natural light, only to be
broken up by a small opening to the west. Dry, green-brown shrubs, some over two
feet high, grow on the bottom of the chasm, the sole vegetation to be found.
name: Bottom of a Chasm

desc:
Oak and fir trees seem to mesh with one another in a small wooded valley, the
branches and leaves overlapping to create a blur of dark vegetation and
blackness beyond. Thorny vines and bristly roots cover the forest floor under
the shadow of the great trees looming above.
name: Forest in a Small Valley

desc:
The canopy and entwined branches of the dark and gnarled trees keep this area of
the valley eternally dark. Gigantic black roots spread out like cobwebs from the
feet of what must be extremely ancient oaks. A wrathful anger is almost
palpable, seeming to emanate from the hateful trees that stand tall and ruthless
above the inhospitable ground beneath them.
name: Sinister Forest

desc:
Old, gnarled trees form a natural barrier as their branches wrap around one
another, twisting into a complex bark-covered mesh. A small puddle has collected
in a depression in the ground, made up of murky black water that continues to
drip from the overhanging trees. Boulders appear to have tumbled down from the
mountains that rise to the west and south, coming to rest violently in the soft
earth beneath the tall trees amid their ruthless strangling roots.
name: Warped Wooded Depression

desc:
Immensely tall, pitch black oaks tower over the stifled dusty ground below. The
sharp ridged bark of the merciless trees seems to carve its way out of the
rot-filled soil, littered with the remnants of smaller vegetation that partially
wasted away long ago but that never fully decayed. The thickness of the great
black roots that burst forth from the rancid ground make even some of the
broader branches look thin by comparison.
name: Blackened Forest

desc:
A great collection of crudely-hewn stumps jut up from the mountainous ground
among many large rocks that lie interspersed with the few fir trees that still
grow in this part of Mirkwood. Some of the stones are blackened with ash, and
the surrounding woods seem to produce a feeling of tenseness. The air is stuffy
and thick with malice.
name: Burnt Mountain Forest

desc:
Few trees remain of what was once undoubtedly a densely forested mountainside.
Numerous trees appear to have been crudely hacked down and limbed here. Evidence
of a recent campfire is apparent, with charred wood in a pile nestled under an
ash-covered boulder. Other blackened rocks are visible with similar traces,
appearing as though they too had been exposed to a recent fire.
name: Scorched Rocks and Hewn Stumps

desc:
Hulking twisting tree trunks interlock with great gnarled boughs and branches to
form an inhospitable wasteland beneath the black lightless canopy of Mirkwood.
Long murderous vines squeeze both root and trunk, sapping life from every living
thing that they touch. Crusted lichen dangles from the serrated bark of the
towering trees, while wicked thorn-filled brush chokes out all other vegetation
from the forest floor.
name: Thorn-choked Wooded Wasteland

desc:
Down in a shallow crack of the forest floor lies a rugged miniature canyon
covered entirely over its top by thick tangled vines. The vines grow so numerous
here that they themselves block all light that might have reached the bottom of
the crack, twisting this way and that along the stone walls as they throttle all
other living things.
name: Vine-covered Crevice

desc:
Loose slimy rocks and sprawling roots cover the ground beneath the sea of trees
that loom dark and ominously above. Shiny, slippery portions of wet roots
protrude at various points from the dark moist soil. The ground becomes
extremely steep to the north as it climbs toward the peaks of the Mountains of
Mirkwood.
name: Rough Mountain Terrain

desc:
Every manner of parasitic vine and creeper have entirely overtaken the forest
here via strangulation and murderous sap-sucking conquest. Thick, gnarled bodies
of strangely long, agile tentacles have forced their way under root and over
boulder, choking all other life from this place in a ruthless and magnificent
display of tangled tortuous takeover.
name: Tangled Nest of Vines

desc:
Dark, enveloping coniferous trees peer over the rising mountain slope facing the
south. Great bulbous root balls grow precariously atop sprawling stone slabs
beneath the menacing trees. Smooth, rocky cliffs form an impassable line to the
east while to the west and north, the forest climbs upward with the mountain.
name: Rising Mountain Slope

desc:
Gloomy pine trees with cold, dry needles grow here atop the lower Mountains of
Mirkwood. Stunted bushes and vegetation struggle to survive in the darkness on
the cold stoney ground. Each tree has broken its way through a tough layer of
bedrock as it took root in some miniscule crack long ago, splitting the stone as
it aged over countless years.
name: Mountainous Forest

desc:
The steep slope is covered with massive boulders that form small crawl spaces
beneath and around various stones, making up a network of tiny tunnels and
crevices in the darkness beneath the canopy of the forest. A large sprawling
field of sharp rocks covers much of the soil around the bases of the trees,
indicating that a landslide occurred here in the recent past.
name: Steep Mountainside

desc:
Small scraggly shrubs grow among withered fir trees that overlook a massive
cliff to the west. Dark boughs loom high above the steep rocky soil surrounding
one great stone peak that rises up into the dense canopy, disappearing in its
dark tangled mass.
name: Forest Peak in the Mountains

desc:
The denseness of the forest even on this lower peak ensures that not a single
ray of sunlight reaches the rocky ground. Towering trees rise upward from steep
mountainsides with their massive roots brutally plunging deep into the stone as
they seek sustenance and stability. Small shrubs cling precariously to steep
stone faces, their roots visible in the small cracks and fissures along the
bedrock.
name: Forested Mountain Peak

desc:
Clumps of withered pines grow here amidst a grove of stumps that have clearly
been hacked apart by axes. Many large rocks cover the ground, covered in
blackened ash and other signs of recent campfires. To the north thick foliage
dominates the forest floor between massive severed tree trunks.
name: Chopped Grove

desc:
Tall dark tree trunks crowd each other on the hillsides in every direction
surrounding a sudden depression that cleaves its way down into the earth. The
cavern opening appears as a black maw, even in the darkness of the thick forest
canopy that prevents natural light from penetrating to the uneven ground below.
name: Hillside Cavern Entrance

desc:
This cavern descends away from a cave mouth to the south. The western side is
lower than the eastern, a continuation of the slanting entrance. Narrow crevices
in the deeper part of the cavern are filled with brackish, silty water. One of
these crevices cuts into the western wall, where it opens into a broad pool.
name: Tilted Tunnel

desc:
A dark pool covers the entire floor of a high-ceilinged chamber. The pool is
shallow in various places where sand bars rise to the surface. Deep crevices
filled with opaque water make it difficult to discern the difference between
shallow and deep areas. The stagnant oily water is occasionally disturbed by
bubbles that ominously rise to the surface from unknown depths below. A gap in
the eastern wall leads to a north-south passage that slants upward away from the
pool.
name: Silty Underground Pool

desc:
This north-south passage slants steeply across its axis. The high side along the
eastern wall is relatively level, making for sound footing. The passage falls
away from this natural path, narrowing eventually into waterlogged crevices. A
few shattered and rotten logs lie in the deep side of the passage.
name: Crooked Creviced Passage

desc:
This passage has an oblong cross section which is slightly tilted so that the
eastern end is higher than the western. Jagged cracks crisscross the walls and
ceiling of the passage, none more than several inches wide. Water seeps from the
cracks, running westward down the slanted passage and into a wide gap that seems
to broaden as it disappears into the ground.
name: Slanted Passage

desc:
Several dark, forbidding openings lead away from this great intersection. Some
of the exits are small, no larger than crawlspaces. Others are so great that an
Oliphant could stand in them. While the cavern's origin is no doubt natural, it
is now the habitat of creatures that dump their refuse in piles along the walls
and create paths that lead to and from the various tunnels.
name: Expansive, Intersected Cavern

desc:
A large natural cavern is worn into the bedrock here by untold years of flowing
water. Frequently used paths are clearly marked on the floor leading off in all
directions, while refuse and unidentifiable junk is scattered in piles along the
walls. A low opening that is rounded and much smoother than the surrounding rock
allows passage to the south.
name: Expansive Cavern

desc:
A cavern opens into a large circular grotto. A set of simple, crude stairs leads
down into a deeper tunnel below. Though this part of the cave may have been
natural in origin, rough work has clearly made the place more habitable. Large
stalagmites have been broken off and ground down to serve as smooth table tops.
The floor appears fairly level, and many of the smaller stone formations have
been hewn away.
name: Atop Simple Stone Steps

desc:
This part of the cavern descends sharply from its entrance to the south,
flattening out into a broad chamber pocked with shallow pools. Water trickles
down the walls and drips slowly from the ceiling. Piles of bedding lie scattered
in the dry spots between pools. Each pool seems filled with sundry pieces of
garbage, filling the air with the stench of rot.
name: Damp Barracks

desc:
The walls of this enormous tunnel-like cavern are lined with deep cracks,
outcroppings, and fallen scree. At a section of the western wall, which is
remarkably smooth compared to the rest of the cavern, a narrow opening leads
into an alcove. There are trampled paths along the cavern floor leading north,
south and into the alcove.
name: Great Cavern by an Alcove

desc:
Jumbled piles of miscellaneous supplies fill a large alcove connected to vast
caverns to the east. Towers of half-full, opened crates sit near the entrance,
their supplies spilling onto the ground. Empty crates line the wall to the west,
tossed in a great heap lacking any sort of order. A layer of sawdust, splinters,
and large planks covers the floor.
name: Cluttered Alcove

desc:
The tall stone walls veer outward here to form a truly massive unlit cavern. The
ceiling is hidden in a shroud of gloom overhead and standing against one wall
reveals nothing about the other side of the cave except blackness. The ground is
surprisingly soft, being apparently made from layers of gravel and sand as well
as mud toward the centre of the cave. The walls narrow to the south, as if much
of the had water drained away into the bedrock.
name: Vast Cavern

desc:
In a slow majestic bend, the enormous cavern wraps itself around a rough wall of
granite to the south-east. The smooth, wet stone floor continues down into the
darkness as it carries on to the south. Shallow pools of dark water along the
centre of the cave, coupled with patterns in the sand, seem to indicate that
water occasionally flows through here.
name: Sloping Cavern

desc:
Much of the ceiling of this vast cavern is lost in gloom. Sharp, glittering tips
of stalactites sprout from the darkness in various locations as water slowly
drips from their tips to land on the cavern's wet floor. The ground slopes from
east to west, showing signs that water recently flowed here. Though the cave
appears natural in its formation, a well-trampled path follows the lowest point.
Small pieces of refuse litter the ground along the subterranean trail.
name: Vast, Natural Cavern

desc:
Scraggly trees rise upward toward the forest canopy above the entrance to an
enormous cavern. Massive stalactites hang down from the low arch of the opening
itself which, together with the trees growing through the stone lip at the
bottom of the entrance appear to form a great gaping maw. The cavern itself
stretches away westward, fading into deep shadow.
name: Broad Cavern Entrance

desc:
The thick, tangled forested hills crowd up against an enormous cavern entrance
leading down into complete darkness. Great trunks rise from the very mouth of
the cave opening, making the pitch black entrance appear even darker than the
rest of the gloomy wood. The soil becomes softer as the ground slopes downward
into the stoney recess.
name: Tangled Hillside Forest at a Cavern

desc:
Tall trees blot out the sky, leaving the hilly terrain below in a heavy
darkness. The tangly roots that emanate from every trunk create large mounds of
tough, gnarled wooden loops that twist and turn into one another. A mist of
smelly spores hang in the air produced by pitcher-like black fungi that have
overrun the forest floor.
name: Looming Wooded Foothills

desc:
This cavern is wide and round, though the ceiling is fairly low throughout. The
floor is made up of rough stone and is covered in crude bedding made from
tattered furs, skins, and pelts. A foul musk fills the air and the stale odour
of sweat mingled with a damp rot emanates from the bedding. The ceiling rises
gently to the immediate north where this chamber joins with a much larger
cavern.
name: Low Barracks

desc:
A gloomy passageway carved from the dark bedrock begins here at the foot of a
set of crude stairs to the west. The top of the stairs is shrouded in darkness
and of the passageway that leads off towards the east no more than a few dozen
feet can be seen before it disappears into inky blackness. Some care was taken
when crafting this tunnel, for while the walls and ceiling are uneven and rough,
the floor is flat and smooth, making for easy travel.
name: Sombre Passageway

desc:
A crude passageway cuts through black shale as it runs east-to-west. Chambers
branch off north and south, their contents hidden in gloomy shadow. A foul
medley of odours lingers in this tunnel, including an acrid burnt smell mixed
with the dank orkish musk and a faint tinge of rot.
name: Juncture in a Sombre Passageway

desc:
This oblong chamber is dozens of yards long east-to-west, yet only at most three
yards wide north to south. A narrow gap in the northern wall serves as the only
exit and the only means for a strong and acrid odour to escape into the tunnels
beyond. Cobwebs cover the walls but it is quite clear that the chamber itself
sees daily use.
name: Bare Sleeping Chamber

desc:
A great chasm cleaves its way through a carved passageway running east to west,
opening suddenly in the centre of the tunnel. Neither the chasm's ceiling or
floor can be seen, hidden by a heavy gloom that shrouds both the height and
depth of the great crack itself. The delvers of this passage carved walkways
into its sides, effectively creating a ring of narrow shelves. The hewn stone
ring creates a strong natural chokepoint at the eastern end where the two paths
meet that has been further fortified with a wooden defensive structure.
name: Sombre Passageway at a Chasm

desc:
Paint-flecked bones hang from the walls and ceiling of a low chamber underground
that is shrouded in complete blackness. A crude wooden table covered in
miscellaneous herbs, animal entrails and strange tools sits at the centre of the
cave, while a recess deep in the eastern wall contains a pot suspended over a
pile of black coals and ashes. The air is slightly hazy and contains an acrid
odour interspersed with the stench of recent death.
name: Smoky Chamber

desc:
Moulds grow in a slithering, oozing pattern down twisted tree trunks in this
hilly region of Mirkwood. Tangled vines weave their way around thorny bushes,
creating choked undergrowth filled with perilous obstacles and razor sharp
thorn-filled thickets. A faint, diffused green glow makes up the only light that
naturally reaches the forest floor during daylight hours.
name: Hilly Forest

desc:
Mixed oak and fir trees grow interspersed atop rolling hills while small shrubs
with withered leaves waste away on the forest floor. Dark stone slabs protruding
through the topsoil combine with the rotting plant matter to blacken the
hillsides beneath the looming trees that cover them.
name: Blackened Forested Hills

desc:
The forest covers rough, mountainous terrain as the slopes of Emyn-nu-Fuin grow
steeper. Large blackened boulders dot the climbing landscape amid countless
twisted trees, each harbouring its own strange perforations in its bark and
lower limbs. The rocky soil supports various small bushes even on its steeper
slopes beneath the mighty oaks and firs that race upward into the dense canopy.
name: Rugged Mountain Forest

desc:
These rocky outcrops are shaded by tall, hoary trees. A canopy of tree limbs
covered with grey lichen obstructs the view of the sky. Cracked boulders sit
between the outcrops, perhaps separated from the crags by the action of wind and
rain. Vines and roots now intertwine with these boulders, continuing the process
of breaking them down into dirt.
name: Shadowed Crags

desc:
Massive, black oak trees loom to either side of a rugged ridge, their gnarled
and sweeping limbs hanging low to the ground. Bone white vines tangle with the
branches, wrapping around the massive trunks, cracked and weeping a dark and
foul smelling sap. Dense shrubs surround boulders atop the ridge.
name: Overgrown Ridge

desc:
Heavily forested, rocky, and craggy ground forms a series of ridges that expand
in all directions. The cliffs to the east are steep and cut short any thought of
travel in that direction. The undergrowth is made up of moss and ferns, with
some larger bushes growing along the edges of narrow ravines where the canopy is
less dense.
name: Shadowed Crags

desc:
Ancient oaks cover these hills entirely, their green canopies blotting out the
sky. A variety of sickly-looking fungi grows on their trunks, on boulders,
roots, and the forest floor. These fungi are black and grey, and a rotten smell
rises from a yellow liquid slowly oozing from them to gather in repugnant pools
on the ground.
name: Shadowed Crags

desc:
Low, rugged mountains rise above Mirkwood. The terrain is rough with jutting
rocks, moss-covered boulders, and small gorges everywhere. Trees with black bark
and knotted roots rise among the boulders to spread their crowns above, casting
the mountains into gloom.
name: Shadowed Crags

desc:
Struggling, sickly trees blanket the slopes of broad, low hills. Their branches
droop to the ground, their wilting leaves spotted with black. The trunks of the
trees are covered in yellow-green fungi which cloud the air with choking spores.
The putrid odour, the mottled bark, and the sagging crowns of the trees combine
to tell a story of rot and decay.
name: Foul, Forested Foothills

desc:
The canting nature of the terrain might be what causes the trees to grow twisted
and bent in odd angles. Vines twist around the trees, covering their bark like
thorny, tangled snakes. A foul and stinking black moss grows across the rocks
and boulders. The slope climbs into a mountain pass to the west, while
descending into a hilly area to the east.
name: Overgrown Slope

desc:
A wide, rugged ridge stretches from the east to the west, while a gentle slope
descends to the south. The terrain makes for very difficult travel, with crags
and cliffs everywhere. Gnarled, twisted trees rise from in-between rocks and
boulders. Although stunted and bent, they hold up massive, sprawling crowns that
form a dense canopy overhead. On the ground, little but moss and ferns seem to
find the dark, stony environment agreeable.
name: Shadowed Crags

desc:
Moss-covered crags and gnarled, ancient trees dominate this region of the
Emyn-nu-Fuin. Layers of dead leaves cover a forest floor shrouded in gloom by
dense foliage above. Half-buried rocks and thick, knotted roots hide under the
leaves. Dense, thorny patches of briar grow in clusters wherever there is a gap
in the canopy.
name: Shadowed Crags

desc:
Jagged boulders and deep, narrow gorges await the unwary traveller in the
shadows under the trees in this part of the Emyn-nu-Fuin. Grey lichen drapes
branches that droop as if the flimsy fungi were of great weight. The forest
floor dips sharply to the west, the rocky terrain disappearing from view beneath
dark canopies.
name: Shadowed Crags

desc:
The steep rocky terrain rises a hundred feet above the forest. These low, rugged
mountains host a plethora of plant life, ranging from moss and small shrubs to
tall, ancient trees. Steep cliffs rise to the west, separating this part of the
Emyn-nu-Fuin from whatever lies on the other side.
name: Tangled Mountain Range

desc:
The terrain ascends from all directions to reach this flat plateau. The ground
is stony with little topsoil and what vegetation grows here is made up of small
shrubs and plants. Several large boulders dot the plateau, moss-covered looming
giants that stand guard over their domain.
name: Wide Plateau

desc:
Sharp and jagged rocks covered in slimy green moss protrude from a broad ridge
that runs from the east to the west. Twisted trees flank the apex of the ridge,
casting shadows on it with their overhanging branches. Dark brown vines hang
from the trees, and roots push their way up through the crumbled rocks atop the
ridge.
name: Overgrown Ridge

desc:
The forest floor descends steeply here, exposing large roots in the earthen
walls of a gully. Through dense foliage and weaving vines, the deep crack
transforms into a larger rift below the base of the forest. A small dark rivulet
steadily runs from above, forming a culvert along the centre of the path.
name: Gully Slope

desc:
Short and spiny thorn bushes cover these low hills, growing thick and wild. A
few elm trees stand defiant along the ridges, their arms swaying slowly
seemingly independent of the wind; faint, rustling sounds are ever present. The
dense vegetation is covered with a parasitic black moss that emanates a foul
odour that carries through the whole area.
name: Brushwood Hills

desc:
Thorny barberry bushes grow thick on the rubble-like hillsides. There is a faint
trail worn into the crab grass between the bushes. The trees that grow on the
floor between hills seem to be mostly gnarled ancients. Sometimes a faint
howling rides on the wind from the north, though if it is caused by air being
forced through narrow gaps and openings or something else is indeterminable.
name: Brushwood Hills

desc:
This cavern begins at a round hole at the top of a slope to the south. From
there, the cavern quickly expands, widening to dozens of yards between the
eastern and the western walls. The floor slants downwards to the north, while
the roof stays at the same height which causes the cavern to expand in height as
well. The walls, roof, and floor are of rough and uneven grey rock.
name: Wide Cavern

desc:
The cave is ovoid with considerably smooth, rock walls of mostly a dim grey
colour, interspersed with ash grey. In a few separate locations, thin, dark
roots protrude from the ceiling, clear evidence that trees or bushes with deep
roots grow above this cave.
name: Large Cavern

desc:
A spacious den has been excavated beneath a hill. The walls look stable and
solid, and are covered with scratch marks. Piles of leaves mixed with animal
hair lie at the back of the den. Some dry, gnawed-on bones litter the floor.
There is no meat on them and they do not seem part of a recent meal.
name: Den under the Hills

desc:
This sombre hallway has a roughly square cross section; though the walls and
floor are somewhat rough, they are far too smooth to have resulted from natural
processes. A jagged, shadowy gap in the northern wall widens into a rugged,
ascending slope. The gloomy hallway continues to the east and to the west, with
no end in sight in either direction.
name: Nether Route

desc:
A long hallway extending from the east meets an apparent dead-end. The western
wall narrows suddenly, tapering to an end as the walls to the north and the
south squeeze inward. Despite the lack of any obvious continuation of the
hallway, a stale breeze carries a foul stench eastward into the dark gloom of
the corridor.
name: Nether Route

desc:
The floor of this hallway is level and worn smooth. Less care was spent on the
walls, which undulate slightly as the passage runs to the east and the west.
There are some faint markings in the smooth, black rock of the floor. A square
has been carved into the centre of passage, along with an arrow pointing
eastward.
name: Nether Route

desc:
Huge slabs of black rock cover the floor of this hallway, each worn smooth. The
walls have been carefully worked to be free of protruding rocks, and the
passageway seems perfectly straight. The ceiling is not very high, perhaps a
deliberate design considering the care taken in the other aspects of this
tunnel. Two massive pillars of rough stone form a frame for an opening to the
south which leads to a steep cave-like passageway; it is a striking contrast to
this corridor.
name: Nether Route

desc:
A dark corridor with a floor of smooth black rock leads into deep gloom to the
east and to the west. It is interrupted only by a narrow opening in its northern
wall where a steep set of stairs ascends to a higher level of these caves. Less
care was taken when crafting the roof than the rest of the hallway, and the
uneven, rugged surface stands in stark contrast to the smooth walls and floor.
name: Nether Route

desc:
This room is a nearly perfect cube, its smooth walls carved with brute force
from the solid rock. The floor has been meticulously flattened and is bare
except for a neatly rolled up pelt in one corner. There are several empty racks
and shelves on the southern wall.
name: Austere Chamber

desc:
The cavernous walls of this steep ravine are heavily worn from erosion, a direct
result of water constantly dripping from the humid forest above. A great crevice
tears through the stone floor of the ravine like a gaping wound rent by some
mighty beast from a forgotten age. Complete darkness shrouds the depths of the
seemingly endless crack, though makeshift paths exist on either side allowing
passage east and west.
name: Bottom of a Ravine

desc:
Foliage begins to grow thick along the ravine floor as water trickling down from
the great twisting roots above makes its way into the soft soil. Slick green
moss covers the ground in uneven patches, producing a musty earthen smell. A
natural overhang has formed in the wall to the north, its exposed stone roof
glistening in the dark from the moisture droplets collecting on its surface.
name: Widening Ravine

desc:
Many dark brown and amber coloured layers of strata appear stacked atop one
another to form the walls of this tiny recess in the ravine to the south. The
belts of colour vary in thickness until, at the very top, all seem to meld into
a dome of beige stone. The alcove is dry but still smells of stifled humid air
and molding vegetation.
name: Layered Alcove

desc:
The tall jagged walls of the canyon race ever upward out of sight into looming
darkness. One side of the fissure towers over the other in a great precarious
overhang, obscuring any meagre glow of light that might have made its way
through the thick forest canopy. The great crack appears to grow shallower
toward the south, revealing the edges of a dark festering pool.
name: Covered Canyon

desc:
Stone rubble piled high along the base of the canyon walls suggests that seismic
activity once formed this great fissure. Moss-covered stones and black slimy
roots protrude from the steep exposed sides, even as a great dark pool of water
covered by a thick layer of indiscernible scum fills the deepest recesses of the
uneven floor.
name: Canyon Floor

desc:
The rough walls of a deep canyon widen as they ascend upward and are covered in
black moss growing thick on their exterior. Bone white roots weave in and out of
the soil, supporting the ancient trees of Mirkwood looming unseen above. A hole
gapes from the western wall while a deep fissure has formed in the eastern face.
Sticky-looking spiderwebs stretch between roots and rocks, too large to be meant
to snare insects.
name: Canyon Crossroads

desc:
The bottom of a deep crevice narrows from north to south amidst a warm, sticky
air that never seems to stir. With limited ground space available, numerous dark
weeds grow ever taller in the rich wet soil as they seek trace amounts of
indiscernible light from the meagre slit of visible forest canopy. An outline of
a large, decaying log can be seen high above, having fallen across the crack in
the earth.
name: Humid Narrow Crevice

desc:
A squat, square chamber sits at the intersection of two passageways. The larger
runs east-to-west and is carved straight and smooth. The other passage runs
north-to-south, and is crudely delved with uneven walls as well as a rough
floor. This chamber appears to be used as a guard post; wooden fortifications
line the west end of the cavern.
name: Guard Post in a Sombre Passageway

desc:
A wide passageway cutting through grey-black shale meets a massive wooden
portcullis guarding the way east. Natural rock formations line the walls and
ceiling, but the floor has been worn smooth. The passage is increasingly covered
in dust and small stones as it approaches the portcullis; beyond it to the east,
visible through the thick hardwood lattice, lie large mounds of debris.
name: Sombre Passageway before a Broken Portcullis

desc:
A spacious chamber far underground appears to serve as a well-stocked armoury
for the orkish forces that dwell here. A collection of brutal weapons hang on
pegs along the walls and stand in wooden racks that rest along the floor in a
ring surrounding the centre of the cavern. Crudely fashioned leather armour
hangs from pegs and is visible within various crates that appear to have
recently been smashed open and then hastily nailed back together by eager
occupants.
name: Well-furnished Armoury

desc:
An underground chamber that was rudely cut from solid rock shows few signs that
attention was paid to aesthetics. The walls and floor are rough and uneven, and
a large pile of fine furs and pelts lies strewn across the western half of the
chamber. Dilapidated leather armour, broken wooden shields, and shoddy stone
weapons litter the rest of the floor. A barren patch of red-stained stone sits
beneath a pair of empty shackles mounted to the eastern wall.
name: Chieftain's Quarters

desc:
Large boulders and jagged rocks of all sizes have fallen in what must have been
a monstrous cave-in blocking the tunnel to the east. The subterranean event has
created a dead-end behind the sturdy iron portcullis to the west, though work
seems to be ongoing to clear the rubble and allow free passage once again.
name: Collapsed Cave

desc:
Wretched boughs blackened by forces unknown twist and warp around each other and
their neighbouring tree trunks amidst a great glade that ever remains as dark as
a moonless night. A sense of great hate and vengeance lingers in the stuffy
still air beneath the baleful branches, which regularly emit foreboding groaning
noises and occasionally produce a loud cracking sound with no visible rhyme or
reason.
name: Baleful Blackened Glade
